name: Proxima Centauri
tagline: The nearest star to the Sun — a flare star with an Earth-size planet next door.
history: Proxima is the closest star to the Sun — the light you see tonight left it 4.24 years ago. It is a small red dwarf, too faint for the naked eye, that erupts in flares powerful enough to challenge any atmosphere. In 2016 astronomers announced Proxima b, a rocky planet at least 1.07 Earth masses orbiting inside the star's habitable zone every 11.2 days — the nearest exoplanet and the closest potentially temperate world to Earth. Whether tidal locking and flares leave it habitable is an open question JWST and next-generation telescopes aim to answer.
